content.title: Snow Makers
content.description: Bài luyện mẫu gồm các dạng câu hỏi Reading, kéo thả đáp án và điền nhãn sơ đồ máy tạo tuyết.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct heading for paragraphs A–C from the list below.

Drag a heading to an answer box, or choose it from the box.

options.content: i. A solution to uncertain weather
iii. How a snow gun works

matchingPairs.answer: i. A solution to uncertain weather
matchingPairs.explanation: Đoạn A giới thiệu vấn đề thời tiết không ổn định và giải pháp là máy tạo tuyết. Heading i bao quát ý chính.
Đoạn B mô tả quá trình hình thành tuyết tự nhiên từ hơi nước đến bông tuyết. Chọn ii.

matchingPairs.answer: iii. How a snow gun works
matchingPairs.explanation: Đoạn C giải thích các bộ phận và nguyên lý hoạt động của máy tạo tuyết. Chọn iii.

questions.questionText:
Match each proposal with the correct researcher, A–C.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

matchingPairs.prompt: Water from melting snow should be used again.
matchingPairs.explanation: “Used again” được diễn đạt bằng “for reuse”. Đề xuất thu gom và tái sử dụng nước là của David Chen (B).

matchingPairs.prompt: Resorts should not add chemicals to the water.
matchingPairs.explanation: Sara Patel đề nghị tránh phụ gia hóa học vì ảnh hưởng đến đất và nguồn nước. Chọn C.

questions.questionText:
Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

Where does the water entering the snow gun come from?
questions.explanation: Nguồn nước là hồ chứa (“reservoir”), tương ứng với phương án B.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the compressor?
questions.explanation: Máy nén cung cấp khí có áp suất vào ống dẫn thứ hai, tương ứng C.

questions.questionText:
Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer?

YES — the statement agrees with the writer

NO — the statement contradicts the writer

NOT GIVEN — the writer's view is not stated

matchingPairs.prompt: Snow guns depend on suitable outdoor temperatures.
matchingPairs.explanation: Máy không tự tạo nhiệt độ lạnh mà phụ thuộc điều kiện ngoài trời. Phát biểu phù hợp, chọn YES.

matchingPairs.prompt: Chemical additives are necessary for responsible snow production.
matchingPairs.explanation: “Necessary” trái nghĩa với “unnecessary” trong bài. Quan điểm của tác giả ngược với phát biểu, chọn NO.

matchingPairs.prompt: The first snow gun was invented in Finland.
matchingPairs.explanation: Bài nhắc đến phát minh máy tạo tuyết nhưng không nêu quốc gia phát minh. Không đủ thông tin để kết luận, chọn NOT GIVEN.

sections.title: Snow Makers
sections.content:
How artificial snow is produced and the environmental questions it raises.

A In the middle of the twentieth century, the growing popularity of skiing made mountain resorts profitable businesses. But resort owners were completely dependent on the weather. If there was not enough snow, they had to close. The invention of the snow gun offered a solution to this uncertainty. Today, snow-making equipment helps many resorts stay open for longer periods, even when natural snowfall is limited.

B Natural snow begins as water vapour in the atmosphere. The vapour condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the temperature is sufficiently low, the droplets freeze into ice crystals. More water particles then join each crystal, producing a snowflake. As a snowflake becomes heavier, it falls towards the ground. Its shape depends on the temperature and moisture of the surrounding air.

C A snow gun achieves a similar result by combining water and air. Water travels from a reservoir through one hose. A compressor supplies pressurised air through a second hose. Inside the machine, a nozzle breaks the stream of water into tiny droplets. A fan spreads these droplets into the cold air, where they freeze before reaching the ground. The equipment does not create cold temperatures; it relies on suitable outdoor conditions.

D Researchers have proposed several improvements to make snow production more sustainable. Engineer Anna Meyer focuses on pumps that consume less electricity. Hydrologist David Chen recommends collecting meltwater and returning it to the reservoir for reuse. Environmental scientist Sara Patel argues that resorts should avoid chemical additives, which may affect soil and local waterways. Their proposals address different costs of producing artificial snow.

E Before switching on a snow gun, operators measure both air temperature and humidity. Cold, dry conditions are generally most suitable because the droplets cool and freeze more quickly. When the air is too warm, artificial snow cannot be produced effectively. Machine-made snow is often denser than natural snow, since its ice particles are smaller and more compact. The quantity of water required varies with the conditions and the desired depth of the snow layer.

F Critics point to the electricity and water consumed by snow-making systems and question their effects on mountain ecosystems. The writer believes that chemical additives are unnecessary for responsible snow production. Better equipment and careful water management can reduce environmental costs, but they do not remove them entirely. Resorts must weigh the value of a longer skiing season against the resources it requires.
